pr_title: Remove Blocks when disk threshold monitoring is disabled
pr_body:
This change ensures that existing `read_only_allow_delete` blocks that 
are placed on indices when the `flood_stage` watermark threshold is 
exceeded, are removed when the disk threshold monitoring is disabled.

This is done by changing how `InternalClusterInfoService` behaves when
disabled. With this change, it will keep calling the registered listeners
periodically, but with an empty `ClusterInfo`.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/86383
pr_comments: Hi @pxsalehi, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

~I'm assuming [this call](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/f02c3c280a39f148298798c6bf2dbd37e7a0ae42/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/routing/allocation/DiskThresholdMonitor.java#L411) is idempotent (with removing existing blocks), and we don't need to consider it in the flow when the disk threshold monitoring gets disabled.~ I guess this is not relevant anymore.

@henningandersen, I tried out the direction suggested, and I came across several issues/concerns:

I tried it out a bit [here](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/88277/commits/c8cf61504b88824ec5ee188373e8f5cc265fc8ae), by adding a new [interface](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/88277/commits/c8cf61504b88824ec5ee188373e8f5cc265fc8ae#diff-6fe0b36a03a9b18dbf7c3276af06485d2ec2e5527d61befc87201a448304e06bR11-R15), that allows cluster info listeners to be called when the cluster info service is disabled. The problem is that I ended up with the same issue as addressed in this PR with the flag, i.e., `ClusterInfoService` might call the `clusterInfoServiceDisabled` of the listener, while the previous operation resulting from the `onNewInfo` call of the listener is still in progress! Making `ClusterInfoService` aware of the in-progress operations of the called listeners, to make the `clusterInfoServiceDisabled` call safe, doesn't seem right to me. That is why currently we use the `checkInProgress` to dismiss potentially parallel calls to the listener.

On the other hand, continuously calling the `clusterInfoServiceDisabled` seems a bit strange to me. Besides the above issue, I'm reluctant to drag this into the `ClusterInfoService` for two reasons:

First of all, the whole separation between the `ClusterInfoService`(`InternalClusterInfoService`) and `DiskThresholdMonitor`, is a bit unclear/leaky, at least to me. E.g., while the the `ClusterInfoService` seems to be intended as a generic service, it is directly controlled by the disk threshold monitoring setting flag, and currently disk threshold monitoring seems to be the only listener that uses the cluster info service. Moving this disable-handling partially there seems to just make this worse.

Secondly, the code in `ClusterInfoService` is rather complicated and from what I can see, has only one test. Moving this logic there seems to not be necessarily more testable.

I do like to revisit the current approach and drill down on the safety concerns. 

I could try to write a test that ensures when the setting is disabled while an `onNewInfo` is in progress, the `removeExistingIndexBlocksIfDisabled` is called after it.

I still don't understand the exact concern or unsafe example.

The flag is used to prevent concurrent `onNewInfo` and `removeExistingIndexBlocksIfDisabled`. `removeExistingIndexBlocksIfDisabled` only runs if it can obtain the flag the same way `onNewInfo` does, and doesn't run if the flag is set by an on-going `onNewInfo`. The call after finishing an ongoing `onNewInfo`, makes sure the cleanup gets another run, to cover the case that it didn't run upon disabling the setting, due to the ongoing `onNewInfo`. Essentially, after each `onNewInfo` (which could add the blocks) we'd run the cleanup step (only if the setting is disabled). If the setting is disabled and the blocks are removed, this means we check the flag which was disabled, and a new `onNewInfo` shouldn't run. And if it does, we check at the end if we need to clean up. Several cleanup calls are idempotent.

> Several cleanup calls are idempotent.

Sort of. One worry is the case where we disable the setting and then quickly reenable it. I'd think we risk the cleanup step removing a block that was added after the setting was reenabled.

> ClusterInfoService might call the clusterInfoServiceDisabled of the listener, while the previous operation resulting from the onNewInfo call of the listener is still in progress!

I can see that being possible yes. I still wonder if just calling it with the empty info is not good enough? I am not sure it has any downsides.

Also, another potential race here is the order of invocation of the setting update consumers. I'd think the order is such now that it does not impose an issue (since `DiskThresholdSettings` must be constructed before `DiskThresholdMonitor`). But relying on that order adds another layer of "hard thinking" when wanting to read through the code and convince yourself it is safe.

> I am not sure it has any downsides.

Is there any other good reason that someone would apply `READ_ONLY_ALLOW_DELETE` blocks to indices when disk threshold monitoring is disabled? If yes, wouldn't having this periodic cleanup calls be troublesome?

This is now ready for review again. I have updated the description with a summary of the approach.

As for my question above, I had a look in the code, and didn't find any other usage of the `READ_ONLY_ALLOW_DELETE` which indicates it could be applied outside of the disk threshold monitoring/allocation scenario. I quickly looked through the docs as well, and to me it seems that this block is intended to be used by the disk-based shard allocator. (https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.3/index-modules-blocks.html)
@DaveCTurner: Since now we rely on changes in `InternalClusterInfoService`, could you please also have a look? Thanks! :-)
Sorry Pooya I've been struggling to find the time to give this the attention it deserves. Perhaps @idegtiarenko can help?

@elasticmachine run elasticsearch-ci/part-1
(Failed yaml test seems unrelated and not reproducible. Opened: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88804)

### OS Version

Linux kibana.q-mex.net 3.10.0-1160.59.1.el7.x86_64 #1 SMP Wed Feb 23 16:47:03 UTC 2022 x86_64 x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Problem Description

Some parts of the internet / stackoverflow / forums, advise to disable the `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.threshold_enabled` setting. This also disables the unlocking if the cluster is in a locked state, effectively creating a perma-lock (until someone changes the setting back). 

This means indices stay locked even after disk usage dropped significantly. This is especially bothersome for indices like `.security` and `.async-search` which do not allow manual intervention.

(Not that big of a deal, having figured out now what caused my lockup. I wanted to create this GH issue for sake of documentation - I'd be OK if this were closed as `wontfix`)

### Steps to Reproduce

- Have a high disk usage to cause the lockup - ideally in a single-node deployment
- Get your disk usage back to normal levels (63% in my case)
- See that nothing happens

### Logs (if relevant)

_No response_
comments:
AFAICT if `cluster.routing.allocation.disk.threshold_enabled` is `false` then Elasticsearch won't even apply the flood-stage index block, but it would indeed not remove any blocks that were in place when you disable disk thresholds. I guess you hit the flood stage and then disabled disk thresholds?

I think we could reasonably remove any existing `index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete` blocks when changing this setting to `false`. We could also just clarify in the docs that disabling disk thresholds also disables the release of these blocks, but that's not as helpful. Marking this for team discussion to see what others think.

Thank you for your quick and useful reply. 

-------

> I guess you hit the flood stage and then disabled disk thresholds?

Correct.

> I think we could reasonably remove any existing index.blocks.read_only_allow_delete blocks when changing this setting to `false`

That does sound like a good solution to the problem we had. I cannot imagine someone wanting to keep the blocks when they disable the thresholds. (Why would someone want to keep their system in a locked state?)

> Marking this for team discussion to see what others think.

:+1:
We (the @elastic/es-distributed team) discussed this today and agreed that removing the blocks seems like the right thing to do.
Hi, @chen-ni , I have added the label by mistake, sorry for the confusion. This one has been assigned to @kingherc and @pxsalehi

review_comments: I worry that doing this on every refresh is potentially kinda expensive and almost always unnecessary. We could be iterating over hundreds of thousands of indices here, doing a couple of map lookups for each one. Is there really no way to do this just once when the monitor is disabled?

We could keep track of it with another flag! The flag (default false) could be set to true (cleanup done) if a successful block removal call has been made. We'd have to reset it on every "normal" `onNewInfo` call (for future disable calls). Is that too ugly!?

I think this works :) I do agree that it's a little ugly to poll for a condition rather than reacting to events as they occur but really it's not a huge deal in this case and the alternatives seem to be quite a lot more invasive.

Yeah. Maybe something to consider for https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88587. I tried [something different](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/88277/commits/c8cf61504b88824ec5ee188373e8f5cc265fc8ae#diff-6fe0b36a03a9b18dbf7c3276af06485d2ec2e5527d61befc87201a448304e06bR11-R15) before, but that would need some support from `InternalClusterInfoService`.

I agree, using the flag makes sense. Evenso, I wonder if it is worth iterating over the blocks directly instead. I.e., something like `state.getBlocks().indices().keySet().stream().filter(...)` instead? I'd expect that list to be much smaller than the full list of indices.

Going through the routing table rather than the blocks directly is also done in [one more place](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/c0bc85522d7a5bca8d8bd58726d917e716efb32c/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/cluster/routing/allocation/DiskThresholdMonitor.java#L380) in this file. What you're suggesting would also apply there I think, if the two are equivalent. Would it be ok to move that to a new PR? I can look into it and do it in both places. Or would you rather I do both in the PR?
I'd prefer to at least do this one in this PR. I'd be happy to defer the other one to a separate PR.
This class is strangely complicated, it took quite some effort to work this change through. I'm probably partly to blame here. I opened https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88587.

> This class is strangely complicated

 Couldn't agree more! 😄
